runs.final_response:
**Verdict: Success. The inventor was Charles Babbage.** The [Analytical engine article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytical_engine) states: “designed by the English mathematician and computer pioneer Charles Babbage.”

Observed route:

1. Opened [Wikipedia](https://www.wikipedia.org/) in a new In-app Browser tab.
2. Entered “Ada Lovelace” and clicked Search. This opened the [Ada Lovelace article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace).
3. Followed its “analytical engine” link to the supporting article.

I completed one attempt without retries, login, edits, or navigation outside Wikipedia. The article tab remains available for independent assessment.

runs.final_response:
Stopped. The completed actions were:

1. Opened a new tab at [Wikipedia](https://www.wikipedia.org/).
2. Searched for “Ada Lovelace” and opened [Ada Lovelace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace).
3. Followed its “analytical engine” link to [Analytical engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytical_engine).

The observed article identified **Charles Babbage**: “designed by the English mathematician and computer pioneer Charles Babbage.”

Tab 1 remains open. No operation is active.

timing_method: Local UTC timestamp immediately before create_thread dispatch to the raw session final-answer emission timestamp. Includes task startup, browser startup, tool initialization, and skill loading. Excludes polling return delay and later cleanup. Wall clocks rather than one shared monotonic clock provide these native boundaries; millisecond log precision and the short pre-call dispatch gap limit precision. Final message create_time marks an earlier generation boundary and is not the final emission boundary.
usage_scope: Exact main benchmark session cumulative counters reconcile with each recorded per-response usage event. Cached input is included in input. Reasoning output is included in output. Separate approval-review sessions, parent coordination, and later cleanup are excluded. Counters do not establish billed cost.
browser_state_limits: Both started new IAB tabs. Cookies, browser cache, profile, renderer lifetime, and provider internals were not cleared or matched to isolated Chrome in the system run. Tab IDs are local to each task, so both reporting tab1 does not establish a shared underlying tab.
limits: The one-attempt and sequential requirements were violated by a coordination race.
Normal desktop CUA/IAB differs from the system custom interface and isolated Chrome.
Desktop context and tool documentation differ from the CLI coordinator context.
The retained native task clicked Search; the system task selected an autocomplete suggestion.
Live website state differed, including donation content and control indices.
Both native model sessions and browser work overlapped. No general speed, architecture, reliability, or dollar-savings claim follows.
No new local-model responsiveness observation is required.
next_recommendation: Demonstrate the current Wikipedia workflow with observed route and source evidence. Present demonstrated feasibility, not general speed or live recovery effectiveness.
